findings.title: Partition lock creation is racy
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py does get then setdefault on partition_locks with no global lock. Two threads adding the same new Partition concurrently can create two different Lock objects and then synchronize on different locks. That breaks the claimed per-partition mutual exclusion for add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed, allowing lost updates and wrong committable offsets, which causes duplicate processing or skipped commits.

findings.title: Unbounded queues with no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates each work queue as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never blocks or returns a backpressure signal, despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure. If workers stall on a slow subscription, the Arroyo poll loop keeps submitting and memory grows without bound, leading to OOM and growing commit lag. poll only emits a gauge.

findings.title: Strategy close shuts down factory-shared pool, breaks rebalance
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and reuses it for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls queue_pool.shutdown which kills all workers. On Arroyo rebalance/reassignment where the old strategy is closed and a new one is created from the same factory, the shared pool is left shut down with dead workers, so subsequent submits pile up unprocessed. Multiple concurrent strategies would also share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit threads double-committing.

findings.title: terminate leaks commit thread
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py sets shutdown_event and shuts down workers but never joins the commit_thread, unlike close. The daemon commit thread keeps running and keeps calling commit_function and mark_committed on the shared OffsetTracker after termination, causing use-after-terminate commits and thread leaks.

findings.title: Worker swallows failures yet commits offsets
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Failed results are therefore treated as completed and the commit loop will commit past them, so failures are never retried and never reach Arroyo DLQ handling. ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows exceptions, so mocking it to raise still gets committed, losing uptime results silently.

findings.title: assert used for control flow on message type
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit uses assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue) to get partition/offset. Asserts are stripped with python -O, leaving partition/offset unbound, and for any non-BrokerValue message the AssertionError is caught by the blanket except and the message is silently dropped without tracking. FilteredPayload also hits assert not FilteredPayload inside decode_payload and relies on the exception path to mark progress, making normal filtering depend on exceptions.

findings.title: wait_until_empty/get_stats miss in-flight work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize, which counts only queued items not the item already removed by get and being processed by a worker. wait_until_empty can return True while offsets are still outstanding, and total_queued metrics undercount. Tests that wait on total_items==0 plus call counts are racy and can pass before processing or committing finishes, hiding ordering and commit bugs.
